expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "An 'is the revenue table empty?' test protects only against total absence. Your failure still had rows and plausible zeros."

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: "Reconciliation detection: compare dashboard revenue against the source-of-record total for each reporting period"

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: "refuse promotion when:" and "Run these before any COALESCE"

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "Source control: a versioned schema/data contract. A rename or removal of the required column must be a breaking change that fails consumer ingestion"

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "required join-match rate falls below its expected threshold", "join cardinality changes unexpectedly", "freshness and historical volume bounds"

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: No mention of the three-week gap or monitoring/alerting as a separate concern

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: Describes what to do but does not explain the relative danger of silent wrongness
